ai.description: *Theloderma pyaukkya* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a mottled, moss-like pattern of brown, grey, and green. It features prominent skin tubercles and distinct, large, dark-pigmented toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Theloderma pyaukkya* is distinguished from similar Indian species by its unique, vivid sky-blue iris, which contrasts sharply with the dark, mottled skin of its head.
ai.habitat: *Theloderma pyaukkya* inhabits primary evergreen tropical forests in hilly regions, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Theloderma pyaukkya* employs a highly effective defensive strategy by remaining motionless, using its mottled, textured skin to blend perfectly into mossy, lichen-covered bark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Theloderma pyaukkya* breeds in tree holes during the monsoon season. Females lay small clutches of eggs, which develop into tadpoles within these water-filled cavities.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Theloderma pyaukkya* is found in the Chin State of Myanmar, specifically within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Theloderma pyaukkya* consists of a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically emitted from within tree holes in forest habitats.
